verses.mystical_translation: The young prince enters his sovereignty; two decades and a quarter meet sixteen years in the city built on the threshing floor. His mother's name echoes the righteous keeper of the covenant threshold.
The son follows the father's path of righteousness—yet builds a boundary. The people's corruption persists even as the throne holds its stance.
The gate that frames ascent receives his building; the wall of departure harbors his ambition. Infrastructure becomes prayer.
Ridge and thicket yield to his vision: strongholds rise where once only rock and growth held the high places.
The Eastern enemy yields to his hand and returns to his coffers what was taken: silver, grain, the substance of survival and exchange. Twice the bargain holds.
Strength flows from the ordered path, from intention turned toward the holy. The sovereign who readies his own way becomes invincible.
His deeds remain inscribed in the double kingdom's archive—the record of what he built, what he conquered, the pattern of his steps.
The circle closes: again the accounting of years. Reign and age mark their measure in the holy city.
The righteous king enters the sleep of the ancestors in David's city. But his son will turn toward fire and foreign altars—the covenant unravels.

contemplative_note: Jotham's reign shows the path of public righteousness met by private restraint: strong infrastructure, military victory, sustained covenant orientation—yet he does not cross the threshold his father's presumption cost. Power and piety need not converge.
